question: What casing and orientation rules generally apply to word messages on signs?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In general, word messages on signs must be aligned horizontally and read from left to right, and they must use the standard wording shown in the MUTCD and the "Standard Highway Signs" publication. Casing rules vary by sign type: on community wayfinding guide signs, destination names must use lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters, while all other word messages on those signs must be in all upper-case letters. Minor layout modifications to word messages are allowed within standardized designs, but shapes and colors are fixed. Standards (mandatory): - "Except as otherwise provided in this Manual, all word messages shall be aligned horizontally across a sign, reading left to right." - "Except as provided in Section 2A.04, all word messages shall use standard wording as shown in this Manual and in the 'Standard Highway Signs' publication (see Section 1A.05)." - "The lettering for destinations on community wayfinding guide signs shall be a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters (see Section 2D.04). All other word messages on community wayfinding guide signs shall be in all upper-case letters." - "Standardization of these designs does not preclude further improvement by minor modifications to the orientation of symbols (see Section 2A.09), width of borders, or layout of word messages, but all shapes and colors shall be as indicated." Guidance (recommended): - Word messages should be as brief as practical and the lettering should be large enough to provide the necessary legibility distance. - For pavement marking word messages of more than one line, the message should read in the direction of travel, with the first word nearest to the road user (a distinct orientation rule for markings, as opposed to signs). Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 2L-3 shows CMS message examples displayed in all upper-case lettering, aligned horizontally and reading left to right, with a note that single-color CMS with pixel spacing greater than 20 mm use all upper-case lettering while full-matrix CMS with finer pixel spacing should use mixed-case lettering where appropriate. [Image 2] Figure 9D-5's accompanying text illustrates the parallel casing rule for shared-use path Destination Guide signs, where destination lettering uses lower-case with initial upper-case letters and all other word messages use all upper-case letters. Citations: - Section 2A.08 Standard §1 (p.45) - Section 2A.08 Standard §2 (p.45) - Section 2D.55 Standard §32 (p.271) - Section 2A.04 Standard §8 (p.40) - Section 2D.55 Guidance §28 (p.271) - Section 3B.21 Guidance §2 (p.575) - Table 2L-3 (p.517) - Figure 9D-5 (p.1082)
gold_answer: Word messages generally read horizontally from left to right. Place, street, and highway names use initial upper-case letters with lower-case letters; other legends use upper-case letters unless another MUTCD provision specifies otherwise.
